Which description correctly defines a gene pool?

options.0: All allele copies at all loci in a defined population
options.1: The alleles carried by one individual
options.2: Only alleles that produce a visible phenotype
options.3: All genes found in every species in an ecosystem

entries.title: A sample has 40 diploid organisms. What denominator is used to calculate the frequency of an autosomal allele?

options.0: 80 allele copies
options.1: 20 allele copies
options.2: 40 organisms
options.3: 160 chromosome pairs

entries.title: In 100 diploid organisms, observed counts are 36 AA, 48 Aa and 16 aa. Which statement correctly separates observation from an equilibrium prediction?

options.0: Direct counting gives p=0.60; the model then predicts 48 heterozygotes
options.1: The 48 observed heterozygotes mean p=0.48 before any allele count
options.2: The 16 aa organisms mean q=0.16, so the model predicts 26.88 heterozygotes
options.3: Matching these counts proves there is no migration or selection

entries.title: Which condition belongs to the Hardy-Weinberg no-change model?

options.0: All genotypes have equal reproductive success
options.1: Alleles mutate at a constant high rate
options.2: Individuals choose genetically similar mates
options.3: A small population experiences random mortality

entries.title: A sample has fewer heterozygotes than expected but similar allele frequencies. Which process could produce that pattern first?

options.0: Non-random mating among similar genotypes
options.1: A guaranteed new mutation in every gamete
options.2: Equal reproductive success among all genotypes
options.3: Perfect random mating in an infinite population

entries.title: A population has p=0.5 before and after a period of inbreeding, but heterozygotes become less common. Which interpretation fits this pattern?

options.0: Mating pattern can change genotype frequencies without an immediate change in allele frequencies
options.1: Inbreeding must create a new allele to reduce heterozygotes
options.2: A fall in heterozygotes requires p to become zero
options.3: Heterozygote frequency and allele frequency are the same quantity

entries.title: What does 2pq represent in the Hardy-Weinberg genotype equation?

options.0: The expected frequency of heterozygotes
options.1: The frequency of the dominant allele
options.2: The expected frequency of both homozygotes
options.3: Twice the population size

entries.title: Under Hardy–Weinberg assumptions at a two-allele locus, 9% of the modeled population is homozygous recessive. What is q?
A sample contains 35 AA, 30 Aa and 35 aa organisms. Which calculation estimates p directly, without assuming equilibrium?
Which process is the ultimate source of a new allele sequence?

options.0: Mutation
options.1: Independent assortment
options.2: Random fertilization
options.3: Genetic drift

entries.title: Which result most strongly supports drift rather than directional selection?

options.0: Small replicate populations change in different, unpredictable directions
options.1: The same allele rises in every large population under the same condition
options.2: A genotype has higher offspring survival in every trial
options.3: Migrants reproduce and populations converge

entries.title: An allele rises after a drought. Which new evidence most directly supports natural selection over a purely random survival explanation?

options.0: A heritable associated trait predicts higher reproductive contribution across replicated drought populations
options.1: The surviving population is smaller than it was before the drought
options.2: The allele is also present at low frequency in one nearby population
options.3: The same number of organisms is counted with a more sensitive detector

entries.title: Which description defines an ecological community?

options.0: Populations of different species living and interacting in an area
options.1: All individuals of one species across its entire range
options.2: Only the non-living conditions in a habitat
options.3: One organism and all of its genes

entries.title: Which evidence most strongly supports competition?

options.0: Both species perform worse together because they draw down the same limiting resource
options.1: Two species are photographed in the same area
options.2: One species consumes the other
options.3: Both species increase when one provides shelter

entries.title: A fungus gains carbon from a plant in both soils. It raises plant growth in nutrient-poor soil but lowers plant growth in nutrient-rich soil. Which net classifications fit the measured outcomes?

options.0: Mutualism in poor soil; parasitism in rich soil
options.1: Commensalism in poor soil; mutualism in rich soil
options.2: Parasitism in poor soil; commensalism in rich soil
options.3: Competition in both soils because carbon is transferred

entries.title: In a simplified coupled cycle, why might predator abundance peak after prey abundance?

options.0: Higher prey availability first increases predator survival or reproduction, whose population response takes time
options.1: Predators always reproduce before prey
options.2: Prey abundance is calculated from predator abundance
options.3: A lag proves climate has no effect

entries.title: Which comparison best supports competition-driven resource partitioning?

options.0: Species use broad overlapping resources alone but narrower, different resources together
options.1: Species use different resources in different continents
options.2: Both species eat the same food and grow equally well together
options.3: One species eats the other

entries.title: A heritable toxin defence reduces predation but costs energy that could support reproduction. Which comparison best tests whether its net advantage changes with predator abundance?

options.0: Compare reproductive success of defended and undefended plants with and without predators
options.1: Compare toxin concentration only in defended plants at one site
options.2: Count predators without measuring any plant survival or reproduction
options.3: Compare two plant species while changing soil, water and predator abundance together

entries.title: What most directly distinguishes primary from secondary succession?

options.0: Whether developed soil and substantial biological legacies remain at the start
options.1: The exact number of years since disturbance
options.2: Whether the first colonist is a plant
options.3: Whether the site will reach a fixed climax

entries.title: A study compares sites of different ages after disturbance to infer change over time, rather than following one site through time. What is a major limitation of this comparison?

options.0: Sites of different ages may also differ in soil, severity, or history
options.1: It requires waiting at one site for decades
options.2: It cannot include any measurements
options.3: It always proves facilitation

entries.title: After a fire, a site retains soil, roots and some seeds. After a glacier retreats, a nearby site initially lacks developed soil. Which classification matches those starting conditions?

options.0: Secondary succession after fire; primary succession after retreat
options.1: Primary succession after fire; secondary succession after retreat
options.2: Primary succession at both sites because disturbance occurred
options.3: Secondary succession at both sites because colonizing species arrive

entries.title: How is population density different from population size?

options.0: Density expresses individuals per unit area or volume; size is the total count within the boundary
options.1: Density is always larger than size
options.2: Size includes only adults while density includes juveniles
options.3: Density measures birth rate only

entries.title: A population starts at 500, with 60 births, 20 immigrants, 45 deaths, and 15 emigrants. What is ending N?
A wildlife count rises from 80 to 120 after a thermal camera replaces visual surveys. Which design most directly estimates how much the method change affects detectability?

options.0: Run both methods over matched places and times, with repeated comparisons
options.1: Treat the 40 extra detections as births in the interval
options.2: Compare thermal counts in winter with visual counts in summer
options.3: Use only the largest count from each method as the population size

entries.title: Why does an exponential population model add more individuals each interval when the positive per-capita rate stays constant?

options.0: The same rate acts on an increasing number of individuals
options.1: Carrying capacity rises automatically every year
options.2: Every individual produces more offspring each year
options.3: Deaths become mathematically impossible

entries.title: Habitat restoration increases food and nesting sites. What is the most defensible prediction?

options.0: Carrying capacity may increase under the new conditions, but must be estimated from later evidence
options.1: K cannot change
options.2: The population instantly becomes equal to the new K
options.3: Exponential growth continues forever

entries.title: Under comparable conditions, populations starting at N=100, 200 and 300 grow by 40, 40 and 30 in equal intervals. Which pattern is consistent with density-dependent slowing?

options.0: Per-initial-individual changes fall from 0.40 to 0.20 to 0.10
options.1: Absolute growth stays at 40 for all three populations
options.2: Per-initial-individual change rises with population size
options.3: The three observations establish an exact carrying capacity of 300

entries.title: What is the most accurate use of the r/K life-history framework?

options.0: A comparative continuum of trait trade-offs under different ecological conditions
options.1: Two fixed categories that every species fits perfectly
options.2: A ranking from inferior to superior species
options.3: A replacement for population data

entries.title: Why can added adult mortality be especially risky for a late-maturing, low-fecundity species?

options.0: Adults are replaced slowly, so population growth is sensitive to adult survival
options.1: The species has no carrying capacity
options.2: Every juvenile survives
options.3: Genetic drift cannot occur

entries.title: A habitat trial aims to improve juvenile survival. Which result would most directly support revising the proposed mechanism?

options.0: Habitat cover improves as planned, but juvenile survival remains unchanged in replicated treated and comparison sites
options.1: The project uses fewer materials than its original budget estimated
options.2: Adult count is larger in one treated site with no baseline count
options.3: The habitat photographs look greener after seasonal rain

entries.title: One neutral marker matches Hardy–Weinberg genotype expectations while the number of different allele forms across monitored loci declines. Which interpretation is strongest?

options.0: Equilibrium at one marker does not rule out diversity loss or demographic risk
options.1: The population has no genetic concern
options.2: Natural selection is impossible
options.3: The marker proves population size is stable

entries.title: Why compare habitat restoration and predator reduction alone and together?

options.0: The design can estimate separate and interacting effects on recruitment
options.1: It guarantees every confound is removed
options.2: It makes monitoring unnecessary
options.3: It proves genetics is irrelevant

entries.title: A population starts at 500. Over one year it records 80 births, 20 immigrants, 60 deaths and 30 emigrants. Which report uses the correct population balance and denominator?

options.0: Net change +10; final N=510; interval per-capita change=0.02
options.1: Net change +40; final N=540; interval per-capita change=0.08
options.2: Net change −10; final N=490; interval per-capita change=−0.02
options.3: Net change +10; final N=510; interval per-capita change=10/510
